title: Support Operations Cost and Performance Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report details verified metrics for 235 support tickets, revealing a total labor cost of $18,704.10. While overall satisfaction is high at 4.13, email support shows a significantly higher reopen rate (19.8%) compared to chat (10.3%). The Gamma team incurred the highest costs, and a specific segment of high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets requires attention.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 235 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.30 minutes and a total labor cost of $18,704.10.
Team Gamma recorded the highest total labor cost at $6,982.84, followed by Beta at $6,466.66 and Alpha at $5,254.60.
Chat support had the longest average resolution time at 83.54 minutes, while phone support was fastest at 67.89 minutes.
The email reopen rate is 19.83%, which is 92.68% higher than the chat reopen rate of 10.29%.
There are 8 tickets in the high-cost low-satisfaction segment, with a reopen percentage of 12.5%.
Resolution times have a median of 66.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 53.34 minutes. The average satisfaction score is 4.13, with 10 missing values.
The 18 distinct agents show moderate concentration, with the top agent handling 20 tickets, representing an 8.51% share of the total workload.

limitations: The cleaning and analysis stages reported validation failures, suggesting potential data quality issues that could affect metric reliability.
Satisfaction scores were missing for 10 tickets, which may bias the overall satisfaction mean.
The analysis assumes labor cost and resolution time data were accurately captured in the source export.
conclusion: Operations show distinct cost and performance variations across teams and channels. The email channel's high reopen rate (19.83%) and the identification of 8 high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets suggest targeted areas for process improvement. Workload distribution among the 18 agents appears balanced, with no single agent handling more than 8.51% of tickets.
